content.value_statement: Distributed systems are hard to split, coordinate, and keep reliable. This skill guides service boundaries, communication choices, sagas, and resilience patterns.
actual_capabilities: Explains service decomposition by business capability and domain boundaries.
Shows API gateway routing and aggregation patterns for service calls.
Compares synchronous REST calls with asynchronous event-driven communication.
Describes saga orchestration with compensation steps for distributed transactions.
Provides circuit breaker guidance for service resilience and failure isolation.
limitations: Provides patterns and examples, not a complete production platform.
Does not deploy services, brokers, databases, or infrastructure.
Requires user-provided domain context to choose correct service boundaries.
Example snippets need security, observability, and operations review before production.

use_cases.title: Split a Monolith
use_cases.description: Plan service boundaries around business capabilities before extracting code from a large application.

use_cases.title: Improve Service Communication
use_cases.description: Choose REST, messaging, or events for workflows that need clear ownership and reliable coordination.

use_cases.title: Review Distributed Transactions
use_cases.description: Design saga steps, compensation paths, and resilience controls for order or payment workflows.

prompt_templates.title: Map Service Boundaries
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to split [application] into microservices. Identify business capabilities, service owners, data ownership, and risky boundaries.

prompt_templates.title: Choose Communication Patterns
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to compare REST, events, and messaging for [workflow]. Recommend communication patterns and explain failure handling.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Saga
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design a saga for [business process]. Include steps, compensation actions, consistency expectations, and operational risks.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Migration Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to review this microservices migration plan: [plan]. Flag coupling, data ownership, resilience, and rollout risks.

output_examples.input: Decompose an e-commerce checkout monolith into services.
output_examples.output: A boundary map with order, payment, inventory, and customer services, plus ownership notes and integration risks.

output_examples.input: Choose communication patterns for order fulfillment.
output: Use synchronous calls only for immediate user-facing validation.
Use events for inventory reservation, payment completion, and fulfillment updates.
Add retries, timeouts, and circuit breakers around remote service calls.

output_examples.output: A saga outline with charge, reserve, confirm, refund, and release steps, including compensation behavior for each failure point.

best_practices: Start from business capabilities and data ownership before choosing service boundaries.
Prefer asynchronous events for long-running workflows and cross-service coordination.
Add timeouts, retries, circuit breakers, tracing, and health checks to every service path.
anti_patterns: Splitting services while keeping one shared database for all writes.
Using synchronous calls for every workflow and creating chatty service chains.
Starting with microservices before the domain boundaries and operations model are clear.

faq.question: Does this skill generate a full microservices application?
faq.answer: No. It provides architecture patterns, examples, and review guidance for designing distributed systems.

faq.question: Can it help decompose an existing monolith?
faq.answer: Yes. It can guide boundaries, ownership, migration sequencing, and strangler pattern planning.

faq.question: Does it cover event-driven architecture?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes Kafka-style event publishing, subscription, and workflow coordination concepts.

faq.question: Does it include resilience patterns?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers circuit breakers, retries, backoff, bulkheads, and failure isolation.

faq.question: Is the example code production ready?
faq.answer: No. The examples need security, monitoring, testing, and infrastructure changes before production use.
